target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators can get stuck in a gateway restart death-loop for the same wedged main session. After the gateway restarts, a persisted aborted main session can keep entering automatic restart recovery instead of being stopped once rapid accepted recovery attempts show that the session needs operator inspection.

The user-visible failure mode is repeated automatic main-session resume across gateway boots, which keeps the gateway focused on the same stuck session instead of leaving the row in a terminal state for inspection.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the durable stop-condition direction from the existing PR and makes main-session restart recovery use the same accepted-attempt fuse style as subagent recovery:

- Adds optional `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` state with `automaticAttempts`, `lastAttemptAt`, `lastRunId`, `wedgedAt`, and `wedgedReason`.
- Reuses the shared `restart-recovery-fuse` helper so main-session and subagent automatic recovery evaluate the same rapid re-wedge pattern.
- Reserves the durable fuse before dispatching the gateway recovery run, then replaces the provisional idempotency key with the accepted run id.
- Rolls back the provisional fuse reservation when gateway dispatch fails before acceptance.
- Records the accepted recovery run id in `restartRecoveryRuns` for lifecycle suppression, while using `mainRestartRecovery` as the primary retry fuse.
- Keeps a legacy marker-derived attempt floor for old rows that already contain `restartRecoveryRuns` but do not yet have `mainRestartRecovery`.
- Accepted recovery run completion now persists its terminal lifecycle patch even when older recovery markers remain, so marker accounting does not leave a successfully recovered session looking `running`.
- Exhausted rows are tombstoned before another resume dispatch, clear `abortedLastRun`, and transition the session to `failed` with terminal timing fields.
- When an exhausted row still has a restart-recovery delivery route, the existing best-effort unresumable-session notice is sent before the row is tombstoned.
- Transcript preflight/read failures do not create durable recovery state, and pre-acceptance gateway dispatch failures roll back provisional reservations.
- Existing subagent recovery state remains owned by subagent recovery; ordinary main/session progress clears stale main restart-recovery state but does not clear `subagentRecovery`.
- The existing in-process `MAX_RECOVERY_RETRIES` remains a transient startup retry/backoff guard and is not the durable cross-boot policy.

Boundaries and non-goals:

- This adds only an optional internal `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery` persistence field for main restart recovery. It does not add public config, wire protocol, credentials/auth behavior, provider discovery behavior, or Telegram/systemd runtime behavior.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle-suppression and legacy-floor state; it is no longer the primary retry fuse for newly accepted recoveries.
- This does not add a new full Telegram/systemd/live-provider loop proof in this local environment. The PR already carries the prior Mantis Telegram Desktop gateway-run proof from the PR discussion, and this update adds issue-specific file-backed runtime coverage through the production restart-recovery entrypoint.
- Another open candidate was visible for the same issue; this update repairs the existing contributor PR and leaves final landing-path choice to maintainers.

## User Impact

Operators get a durable automatic recovery stop condition across gateway restarts. A wedged main session that rapidly re-wedges after two accepted automatic recovery dispatches is tombstoned before a third automatic resume, while deterministic transcript failures and gateway dispatch failures before acceptance do not consume the durable attempt budget.

After inspection, normal main-session progress can clear stale main restart-recovery metadata without erasing independent subagent recovery tombstones.


- Durable stop condition: main-session restart recovery now persists timestamped accepted-attempt fuse state in `mainRestartRecovery` and evaluates the same two-minute rapid re-wedge window style as subagent recovery.
- Accepted-dispatch charging: recovery dispatch first persists a provisional durable attempt keyed by the idempotency key, successful acceptance replaces it with the accepted run id and lifecycle marker, and failures before acceptance roll the reservation back.

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.title: fix(slack): suppress progress chrome sends
target.body:
## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of chat.postMessage
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: `pnpm test`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Evidence
- `CI=true pnpm oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/send.ts extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts extensions/slack/src/blocks.test-helpers.ts`
- `CI=true pnpm vitest run extensions/slack/src/send.identity-fallback.test.ts` (15 tests)
- `CI=true pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `git diff --check`

## Verification
- Thread-scoped progress chrome converts to `reactions.add` instead of `chat.postMessage`.
- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji remain sendable.

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel agent runs when source messages are recalled
target.body:
Related: #55691
Related: #81997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could recall or withdraw a message but OpenClaw would still continue processing that source message and run the agent/tools. This could happen when the recall event arrived while the original message was already debounced, queued, or inside an agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu recall handling previously only showed up indirectly at reply delivery time, when sending a reply to a missing/recalled message could fail. This change handles the inbound `im.message.recalled_v1` event at the channel boundary, records the recalled source message in a Feishu-local runtime context, skips recalled messages before dispatch, and binds active dispatches to an abort signal so in-flight runs stop instead of producing replies.

Live testing also showed that some Feishu app configurations may not deliver `im.message.recalled_v1` to the plugin, while Feishu's message reaction API still returns code `231003` (`message not found / maybe deleted`) when the typing target is the recalled source message. The Feishu dispatcher now treats that specific channel-local signal as a conservative fallback only when the missing typing target is the inbound source message, then reuses the same recall registry, abort signal, and reply-suppression path.

The state is process-local and bounded because it only needs to coordinate nearby receive/debounce/dispatch timing within one gateway process. It does not add a core API or persistent storage surface.

## User Impact

When a Feishu user withdraws a message, OpenClaw now treats that source message as cancelled. Pending debounced messages are dropped when the recall event is delivered, active single-agent and broadcast dispatches receive an abort signal, and final replies are suppressed if the recall or missing-source fallback lands before delivery.

Closes #99390

AI-assisted: yes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the model-catalog warning loop where generated plugin catalog sidecar writes can fail while the private fs-safe store is protecting `catalog.json`. The reported failure is `FsSafeError: directory changed during operation`; when it lands at the generated catalog write boundary, the sidecar file can remain unwritten and dynamic provider rows stay stale or unavailable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix now covers the owner-side write boundary directly:

- `writeModelsFileAtomicForModelsJson` reopens and retries the private store once when fs-safe reports a transient directory identity swap (`path-mismatch`) or when the same replacement race surfaces as `ENOENT` / `ENOTDIR` during the write.
- Generated plugin sidecar writes and read-only persisted catalog scans for the same agent directory share the existing process-wide model catalog file I/O queue, so readers no longer observe the sidecar tree mid-refresh.

The retry remains narrow: non-transient fs-safe failures such as denied paths still fail without retry. No provider catalog schema, runtime config, plugin SDK surface, dependency, or migration shape changes.

## User Impact

Gateway model-catalog refreshes can recover when a generated plugin catalog directory is replaced during the atomic private-store write. Dynamic provider discovery should be able to publish the refreshed sidecar instead of repeatedly logging the catalog load warning while leaving provider rows stale.

target.body:
Related: #99645

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on chat-style surfaces could receive no visible answer when a Codex-native command approval was declined and the attempt only recorded a tool error. That empty user-addressed turn could be classified as successful terminal progress instead of a non-deliverable terminal failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attempt terminal classifier now requires real delivery/progress evidence, such as assistant text, committed message delivery, synthesized payloads, heartbeat responses, accepted session spawns, client tool calls, yields, or async-started tool activity. A bare `lastToolError` still remains available to payload and retry logic, but it no longer proves that the user received a terminal answer.

Codex app-server trajectory finalization now applies the same non-deliverable rule for empty tool-error completions. target.title: fix(security): exclude test files from plugin code-safety scans (#82469)
target.body:
## Summary

`getCodeSafetySummary` in `src/security/audit-extra.async.ts` scans bundled plugin source via `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` but never passes `excludeTestFiles: true`. The option is already supported end-to-end by `skill-scanner.ts` (`TEST_FILE_NAME_PATTERN`, `TEST_DIRECTORY_NAMES`, plumbed through `walkDirWithLimit`) — it's only the caller in `audit-extra.async.ts` that leaves it off.

As a result, the deep audit (`openclaw security audit --deep`) scans plugin `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` files and produces **critical** `env-harvesting` false positives. Test files legitimately reference `process.env` for fixtures, and `fetch(` / `.post(` strings can appear inside `it("…")` descriptions or mocks; the rule fires on any file containing both, even though test files never load as the plugin runtime entry.

The reporter (operating Evolve, which relays `openclaw security audit --deep --json` findings as alerts) sees stock OC-bundled channel plugins flagged as `CRITICAL: contains dangerous code patterns`, which erodes trust in real findings.

## Fix

Two-line change in `getCodeSafetySummary`: pass `excludeTestFiles: true` to both `scanDirectoryWithSummary` call sites (cache-miss and no-cache paths). Plugin code-safety scans the runtime entry tree by design; test sources don't load at runtime and should not be scored as production credential paths.

This matches the scope the reporter recommended ("option #1") and the existing scanner contract.

Out of scope (the reporter's options #2 and #3 — making `requiresContextWindowLines` a hard gate, masking string literals in addition to comments) are rule-engine changes that touch shipped detection semantics; deferred for a separate maintainer-blessed change.

## Tests

Adds two regression tests to `src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts`:

- **spy-based** — verifies `excludeTestFiles: true` reaches `scanDirectoryWithSummary` for every plugin code-safety call site (caller-contract regression guard).
- **behavior-based** — runs the real (unmocked) scanner against a tmp plugin with a clean `index.js` plus a `provider.proxy.test.ts` containing `process.env.OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL` and `fetch("http://example.test/metadata")`, and asserts no `plugins.code_safety` findings are reported. This is the end-to-end fix-the-symptom test.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Deep plugin code-safety audit flagged `*.test.ts` files inside bundled plugins with critical `env-harvesting` findings (combination of `process.env` and `fetch(` / `.post(`) even though those files never load as the plugin runtime entry. This patch routes plugin scans through the existing `excludeTestFiles: true` option so test sources are skipped, matching the scanner's documented test-exclusion semantics.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, on branch `fix/code-safety-exclude-test-files-82469` at head `70bbd01976`, against upstream `main` at `b05fcad7a7`. Tests exercise the real `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` against real on-disk fixtures created in `os.tmpdir()` (no mocked-scanner result for the behavior test), so the assertion is on the actual production scanner output, not on a mock.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.ts src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

Evidence after fix:

Real vitest run output, exercising the actual `skillScanner.scanDirectoryWithSummary` against a real plugin fixture on disk (no mocked scanner result for the behavior test):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/audit-extra.async.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.6 /Users/jinrui/Desktop/openclaw

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
   Start at  18:06:30
   Duration  283ms
```

The two new tests (`passes excludeTestFiles: true to the skill scanner for plugin code-safety scans (#82469)` and `does not flag process.env + fetch( in plugin *.test.ts files (#82469)`) pass alongside the five pre-existing tests in the same file. The behavior test creates a tmp plugin with:
- `index.js`: empty `export {};` (clean runtime entry)
- `provider.proxy.test.ts`: `process.env.OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_URL;` and `fetch("http://example.test/metadata");` (the exact patterns the reporter cites as triggering false positives)

…then calls `collectPluginsCodeSafetyFindings({ stateDir: tmpDir })` and asserts `findings.filter(... title.includes("test-file-noise"))` returns `[]`. With the fix removed locally, the same test fails with a critical `env-harvesting` finding pointing at `provider.proxy.test.ts:2`, which reproduces the bug shape from the issue.

Also verified independently:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts` — `Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 19 passed (19)` (no regression in the underlying scanner).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` — `Found 0 warnings and 0 errors`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0, 0 errors.

Observed result after fix: The deep audit no longer produces `plugins.code_safety` critical findings sourced from `*.test.ts` / `*.spec.ts` / `*.mock.ts` files or files inside `__tests__/`, `__mocks__/`, `__fixtures__/`, `test/`, `tests/` directories (per `TEST_DIRECTORY_NAMES` in `skill-scanner.ts`). Production runtime files are still scanned exactly as before. The `excludeTestFiles` semantics already in place for `skill-scanner.ts` are now actually applied to the plugin code-safety code path.

What was not tested: Live run against the reporter's exact `discord` channel plugin (the bundled fixture is large; the regression test instead uses a minimal plugin reproducing the same trigger pattern from the same kind of file). Effect on installed-skill code-safety scans was not changed here — the same `getCodeSafetySummary` is used by `collectInstalledSkillsCodeSafetyFindings`, so installed skills now also get test-file exclusion; this matches the conceptual contract (skill runtime entry, not its specs) but the issue is plugin-focused so installed-skill end-to-end was not separately re-verified. Options #2 (hard-gate `requiresContextWindowLines`) and #3 (mask string literals) from the issue are deferred.

target.title: fix(line): cap user profile cache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an unbounded in-process **`userProfileCache`** in the LINE send path (`extensions/line/src/send.ts`). Profile lookups are cached for 5 minutes (TTL) but had no entry-count cap, so gateways serving many distinct LINE users accumulate Map entries indefinitely.

**Concrete scenario:** A LINE gateway processing inbound messages from 10 000 distinct users over several hours caches each `getUserProfile` result. With no size cap, the cache grows to 10 000+ entries and does not shrink until the gateway restarts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extracts a `cacheLineUserProfile` writer helper that:

1. Deletes the existing entry for `userId` when present (refreshes insertion order for re-fetched profiles)
2. Sets the new profile entry (newest insertion position)
3. Calls `pruneMapToMaxSize` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`) to evict the oldest-inserted entry until the map is at or under **1 024 entries**

The cap constant `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024` is wired only in `cacheLineUserProfile`; TTL logic in `getUserProfile` is unchanged.

**Eviction semantics:** The cache uses insertion-order-on-write eviction, not pure LRU. Entries are moved to newest position when they are re-fetched from the LINE API (TTL miss or force-fetch). Read-only cache hits do not refresh insertion order, so a valid cached profile that has not been re-fetched can be evicted when 1 024 newer distinct users fill the cache. This is the documented behavior of `pruneMapToMaxSize` (first iterated entry → oldest insertion → evicted first) and is an acceptable trade-off for bounded memory without scan overhead on every read.

## User Impact

**Before:** Long-lived LINE gateways accumulate one `userProfileCache` entry per distinct user indefinitely, growing Map memory without bound.

**After:** The cache is capped at 1 024 entries. Entries evict in insertion order once the cap is exceeded. A re-fetched profile is refreshed to newest position; a cache hit does not change its eviction rank. Behavior is unchanged for the first 1 024 distinct users seen in a gateway lifecycle.

## Evidence

- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:28` — `LINE_USER_PROFILE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 1024`
- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:33–43` — `cacheLineUserProfile`: delete + set + `pruneMapToMaxSize`
- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:524` — `getUserProfile` now calls `cacheLineUserProfile` instead of bare `userProfileCache.set`
- `extensions/line/src/send.ts:540–542` — `resetLineUserProfileCacheForTests` export (test isolation only)
- `src/infra/map-size.ts:13` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` iterates insertion order and deletes the first key until the map fits
- Diff: +39/−1 across 2 files (source +17, tests +21, plus one `beforeEach` reset line)

### Behavior proof

All tests below were run against PR head commit `aaf69e5d98116c41a40206f3b0f66aaaef4271a0` on Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2 (macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64, 2026-07-08T05:24:12Z). The SHA can be independently verified:

```bash

# aaf69e5d98116c41a40206f3b0f66aaaef4271a0
```

#### 1) Profile cache eviction regression — targeted verbose

```text
 ✓ |extension-line| extensions/line/src/send.test.ts > LINE send helpers > evicts oldest profile cache entries once the cache exceeds its cap 23ms
 ↓ |extension-line| ... > (12 other tests skipped)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

   Start at  13:24:12
   Duration  909ms (transform 402ms, setup 91ms, import 3ms, tests 752ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.70s
```

Regression flow:
1. Fetch `U-first` → `getProfileMock` called **1×** (cached at insertion position 0)
2. Fetch `U-fill-1` … `U-fill-1024` → **1024** more API calls (**1025** total; cache now at cap 1024 with `U-first` evicted)
3. Re-fetch `U-first` → `getProfileMock` called **1×** again, confirming the entry was evicted and not still cached


target.title: feat(session-lock): opt-in diagnostics for embedded session fence takeovers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opt-in observability for embedded-attempt **session fence takeovers**.

When a session `.jsonl` changes under a released prompt lock in a way the fence cannot explain as an owned in-process write, the controller tears the attempt down by throwing `EmbeddedAttemptSessionTakeoverError` — which carries only the file path. Across the **10 takeover throw sites** in `attempt.session-lock.ts` there was previously **no diagnostic at all** (the file has no logger). In production this makes a takeover effectively opaque: the only way to learn *which* check tripped and *what* file state could not be reconciled was to patch the installed bundle and add logging by hand.

The gap is real. A released-prompt takeover can fire when a legitimate in-process writer (e.g. an outbound delivery-queue transcript append) races the fence window, and without the fingerprints and owned-write history it looks identical to a genuine external editor.

## What Changed

Every takeover-detection point now goes through a small `markSessionTakeover(reason, current?)` helper. **Behaviour is unchanged** — it sets the same `takeoverDetected` flag and the same error is still thrown. When `session-lock` debug logging is enabled it additionally emits one structured record:

- `reason` — which check tripped (`unexplained-session-file-change`, `owned-write-merge-rejected`, `write-lock-acquire-error`, …)
- `sessionFile`, `fenceActive`, `fenceGeneration`
- `expectedFingerprint` vs `currentFingerprint` (dev/ino/size/mtimeNs/ctimeNs, stringified so the record survives any JSON transport)
- `ownedWriteCount` and `lastOwnedWriteGeneration`

It is gated behind `isEnabled("debug")`, so there is **zero overhead when the subsystem is not in debug**. No new env var — it uses the existing `session-lock` subsystem logger.

## Evidence

**Live diagnostic output.** Exercising a real external-append takeover (append to the session file while the prompt lock is released, then take the write lock) now emits, via the `session-lock` logger:

```
embedded session fence takeover: unexplained-session-file-change
{
  "reason": "unexplained-session-file-change",
  "sessionFile": ".../session.jsonl",
  "fenceActive": true,
  "fenceGeneration": 1,
  "expectedFingerprint": { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "19", "mtimeNs": "1783519408483846902", "ctimeNs": "1783519408483846902" },
  "currentFingerprint":  { "exists": true, "dev": "16777231", "ino": "200684408", "size": "63", "mtimeNs": "1783519408484811232", "ctimeNs": "1783519408484811232" },
  "ownedWriteCount": 0,
  "lastOwnedWriteGeneration": null
}
```

The record immediately tells the story: **same inode**, size grew `19 → 63` (a plain append), `ownedWriteCount: 0` — an unpublished writer advanced the file. That is exactly the signal needed to distinguish a benign in-process append (which would carry an owned-write generation) from a real external editor.

**Tests.** New `attempt.session-lock.diagnostics.test.ts`:
- emits the structured diagnostic (reason + fingerprints) on a real takeover,
- stays silent when `session-lock` debug logging is disabled (zero overhead),
- stays silent when no takeover occurs.

The full existing `attempt.session-lock.test.ts` suite (222 tests) passes unchanged, confirming the flag/throw behaviour is untouched. `oxlint` and a scoped `tsgo --noEmit` are clean on the changed files.

target.title: [Bug]: Agent heartbeat routes to wrong agent's session instead of its own
target.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary


Configured agent's heartbeat executes in default agent's session regardless of isolatedSession setting

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an agent with a heartbeat configuration:

```json
{
  "name": "historian2",
  "heartbeat": {
    "every": "10m",
    "activeHours": { "start": "00:00", "end": "24:00", "timezone": "Asia/Tokyo" },
    "includeReasoning": true,
    "target": "discord",
    "directPolicy": "allow",
    "to": "user:discord-user-id",
    "lightContext": false,
    "isolatedSession": true,
    "skipWhenBusy": false
  }
}
```

2. Put a unique logging command in ~/.openclaw/workspace-historian2/HEARTBEAT.md:

```
the agent must execute following command `mkdir -p /home/node/.openclaw/workspace-historian2/logs && date >> /home/node/.openclaw/workspace-historian2/logs/heartbeat.log`
```

3. Put a different logging command in the default workspace's HEARTBEAT.md:

```
the agent must execute following command `mkdir -p /home/node/.openclaw/workspace/logs && date >> /home/node/.openclaw/workspace/logs/heartbeat.log`
```

4. Wait for the heartbeat to fire (or trigger manually with openclaw system event --text "..." --mode now)

5. Check which workspace's HEARTBEAT.md was executed


### Expected behavior

When an agent (e.g., `historian2`) has a heartbeat configured, the heartbeat should execute **in that agent's own session** and read **that agent's own `HEARTBEAT.md`** from its workspace.

### Actual behavior

The heartbeat executes in the **default agent's session** (`main`) and reads the **default agent's `HEARTBEAT.md`** instead of the configured agent's `HEARTBEAT.md`. This is a **routing bug**, not a prompt or model accuracy issue.

### OpenClaw version

v2026.6.11

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04LTS

### Install method

docker

### Model

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (LM Studio)

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw->docker bridge->home lan->Other Windows PC's LM Studio

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

### Key findings

- isolatedSession: true — historian2's session directory is empty (ephemeral), default's logs/heartbeat.log was created
- isolatedSession: false — same result: historian2's logs/heartbeat.log was NOT created, default's logs/heartbeat.log WAS created
- Both settings produce the same result: the default agent's HEARTBEAT.md is executed
- openclaw status --deep shows Last heartbeat: ok-token · discord, confirming the heartbeat ran successfully — just in the wrong agent's session

### `openclaw status --deep` output

│ Heartbeat │ disabled (main), disabled (historian), 10m (historian2) │
│ Last heartbeat │ ok-token · 1m ago · discord │

### Additional evidence

- `openclaw system heartbeat last` shows `"status": "skipped"` when `target: "last"` (no last session exists)
- Changing `target` to `"discord"` resolved the skip issue
- Historian2's session directory is empty (only `sessions.json`), confirming isolated sessions are ephemeral
- The heartbeat turn log appears in the **default agent's session directory**, not historian2's


### Impact and severity

- Multi-agent setups where each agent has its own `HEARTBEAT.md` will not work as documented
- Agents cannot have independent periodic tasks via heartbeat
- The documented behavior ("Heartbeats run in the agent's main session by default") does not match actual behavior

- `openclaw system heartbeat last` shows `"status": "skipped"` when `target: "last"` (no last session exists)
- Changing `target` to `"discord"` resolved the skip issue
- Historian2's session directory is empty (only `sessions.json`), confirming isolated sessions are ephemeral

The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

## Verification

- Progress chrome without a reaction target is suppressed before Slack post.
- Semantic replies using the same leading emoji remain sendable.

target.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #93069.

This keeps the config contract honest without stranding existing configs:

- `diagnostics.otel.protocol` now documents and validates the only implemented transport: `http/protobuf`.
- Existing shipped configs with `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` are now handled by `openclaw doctor --fix` instead of simply becoming invalid on upgrade.
- If the old config also had telemetry enabled, doctor disables `diagnostics.otel.enabled` while removing `protocol`, preserving the old runtime behavior where `grpc` never exported telemetry.
- `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` remains a fail-closed runtime override path, and now has focused regression coverage.
- Real gRPC exporter support is intentionally out of scope here.

## Linked context

Closes #93069.

Related review concern: ClawSweeper flagged the first version because it rejected a shipped config value without an upgrade path. This revision adds that doctor migration path and proof.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs no longer get stranded by the stricter schema; doctor removes the unsupported protocol and disables enabled telemetry until the operator chooses an OTLP/HTTP collector.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, Node v25.6.1, branch head `074f6a0b45`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module -e '
  const { validateConfigObjectRaw } = await import("./src/config/validation.ts");
  const { migrateLegacyConfig } = await import("./src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.ts");
  const input = { diagnostics: { otel: { enabled: true, endpoint: "http://otel-collector:4317", protocol: "grpc" } } };
  const before = validateConfigObjectRaw(input);
  const migrated = migrateLegacyConfig(input);
  const after = validateConfigObjectRaw(migrated.config ?? {});
  console.log("before.ok=" + before.ok);
  if (!before.ok) console.log("before.issue=" + before.issues.find((issue) => issue.path === "diagnostics.otel.protocol")?.message);
  console.log("migration.changes=" + JSON.stringify(migrated.changes));
  console.log("after.config=" + JSON.stringify(migrated.config?.diagnostics?.otel));
  console.log("after.ok=" + after.ok);
'
```

- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```text
before.ok=false
before.issue=Invalid input: expected "http/protobuf" (allowed: "http/protobuf")
migration.changes=["Removed unsupported diagnostics.otel.protocol \"grpc\"; use \"http/protobuf\" with an OTLP/HTTP collector.","Disabled diagnostics.otel.enabled because legacy grpc configs never exported telemetry; re-enable it after choosing an OTLP/HTTP collector."]
after.config={"enabled":false,"endpoint":"http://otel-collector:4317"}
after.ok=true
```

- Observed result after fix: The unsupported `grpc` config is rejected by validation before migration, doctor migration removes `protocol`, disables enabled telemetry, keeps the endpoint intact, and the migrated config validates successfully.
- What was not tested: A live OTLP collector or real telemetry export; real gRPC exporter support is not implemented by this PR.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The direct proof imports the actual config validation and doctor migration modules from the source checkout. The runtime env override path is covered by the focused diagnostics-otel service test below rather than by a live collector run.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): ClawSweeper’s earlier review reproduced the issue by source inspection and flagged the lack of a doctor/migration path for shipped `grpc` configs.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrate.test.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/deprecation-compat.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test.ts src/commands/doctor-config-flow.test-utils.ts src/config/validation.allowed-values.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts`
  - Passed: 5 Vitest shards, 343 tests.
- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

Regression coverage added:

- Doctor migration removes `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` and disables enabled telemetry.
- Doctor preflight reports shipped `grpc` configs as repairable legacy config.
- Doctor config flow applies the repair end to end.
- Config validation reports the allowed value as `http/protobuf`.
- Diagnostics OTel service rejects `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc` before exporter startup.
- Deprecation compatibility inventory tracks the migration so it is not deleted accidentally.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes` — unsupported `grpc` config now fails validation, with doctor repair for existing configs.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `Yes` — schema narrows to `http/protobuf`, and doctor migrates legacy `grpc` configs.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `No`.

Highest-risk area: upgrade behavior for existing `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` configs. The doctor migration is intentionally conservative: it preserves the old no-export outcome by disabling telemetry when the unsupported `grpc` config had been enabled.

## What Problem This Solves

Runway video generation previously ignored `models.providers.runway.request` overrides (headers, allowPrivateNetwork, dispatcherPolicy). Users who configured a request policy for Runway saw it applied to chat/completion providers but not to video generation, so private-network access, custom headers, and dispatcher routing were dropped on the floor.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mirror the pattern already used by `openai`, `pixverse`, `google` image generation, and Alix-007's recent DashScope/MiniMax/OpenRouter video request-policy PRs: resolve the configured transport policy once and carry it through every HTTP stage of the video operation.

## Changes

- `extensions/runway/video-generation-provider.ts`

  - Forward the sanitized request policy to `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig`.
  - Pass the resolved `allowPrivateNetwork` and `dispatcherPolicy` into `pollRunwayTask` and `downloadRunwayVideos`.
  - Use guarded fetch helpers for status polling and generated-video download when the resolved policy includes `allowPrivateNetwork` or `dispatcherPolicy`, falling back to the existing unguarded helpers when no guarded options are needed.

  - Expand the regression test to assert that configured headers, `allowPrivateNetwork`, and `dispatcherPolicy` reach create, poll, and download stages.

target.title: fix(doctor): normalize legacy Google provider config to current catalog schema
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102138 — legacy `models.providers.google` blocks silently fail catalog
validation, making all `google/*` models unavailable with 120s idle timeouts.

## Root Cause

Older Google provider config blocks lack three fields required by current schema:
1. Missing `api: "google-generative-ai"`
2. `input` includes unsupported `audio`/`video` modalities
3. Missing `cost.cacheWrite`

## Fix

Add `normalizeCompatibilityConfig` in the Google plugin doctor contract:
1. Backfill `api = "google-generative-ai"` if missing
2. Coerce model `input` to `["text", "image"]`
3. Backfill `cost.cacheWrite = 0` if missing

Uses `structuredClone` pattern consistent with other plugin doctor contracts.

## Evidence

### End-to-End Proof: `openclaw doctor --fix`

```
BEFORE: api=none, input=[text,image,audio,video], cacheWrite=none
AFTER:  api=google-generative-ai, input=[text,image], cacheWrite=0
```

Doctor detected and repaired all three fields in one pass.

### Regression Test

Added `extensions/google/doctor-contract-api.test.ts` (8 tests):
- `backfills missing api` — verifies `api = "google-generative-ai"` is set when missing
- `coerces input modalities to text and image` — verifies audio/video removed
- `backfills missing cost.cacheWrite` — verifies `cacheWrite = 0` added
- `repairs all three legacy fields in one pass` — combined scenario
- `preserves existing apiKey and baseUrl` — verifies existing fields survive
- `leaves already-valid Google config unchanged` — idempotency
- `leaves config without Google provider unchanged` — no-op for non-Google configs
- `does not mutate the input config` — immutability guarantee

### Source-Level Proof

```
normalizeCompatibilityConfig(cfg) →
  api: google-generative-ai
  input: [text, image]
  cacheWrite: 0
```

target.title: fix: preserve Telegram bare URL query separators
target.body: Closes #102162 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where Telegram users receiving a bare URL with multiple query parameters could see or open an inline-link destination containing a literal `&` when the agent reply was rendered through Telegram HTML/rich formatting. This affected ordinary model replies such as `https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit` when Telegram linkification turned the visible bare URL into an inline HTML link. ## Why This Change Was Made Telegram now leaves bare HTTP(S) URLs containing raw query separators as decoded text instead of wrapping them in an inline `` marker; labelled Markdown links still use inline-link markup and keep attribute escaping. This keeps the fix local to the Telegram formatter rather than changing the shared Markdown renderer or Slack formatting behavior. Risk note: this touches Telegram channel formatting, so the regression tests cover the plain Markdown, rich HTML, and chunked Telegram render paths, plus the labelled-link non-regression; Slack formatter and shared renderer tests were also run to check sibling behavior. ## User Impact Telegram users should receive bare multi-parameter URLs that preserve the intended raw `&` separator after Telegram parses the HTML text, so tapping the URL does not lose the later query parameters. Users can still send labelled Markdown links as before. ## Evidence Before on current main (`4bf70be01a`), the real Telegram formatter produced an inline link whose href and visible label both contained `&`: ```text https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit ``` After this change, the same real formatter entry points keep the bare URL as Telegram HTML text, while labelled links still render as anchors: ```text markdownToTelegramHtml: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit markdownToTelegramRichHtml: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit markdownToTelegramChunks: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit labelled link: edit ``` Telegram Bot API documentation for HTML parse mode says `&` in text must be sent as `&`, and the MessageEntity contract distinguishes normal `url` entities from `text_link` inline links. A live `getMe` check against the configured Telegram Bot API token returned HTTP 200 with `ok: true`; no token or bot identifier is included here. Commands run: ```text node --import tsx -e 'import { markdownToTelegramHtml, markdownToTelegramRichHtml, markdownToTelegramChunks } from "./extensions/telegram/src/format.ts"; const input="https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit"; console.log(JSON.stringify({html: markdownToTelegramHtml(input), rich: markdownToTelegramRichHtml(input), chunked: markdownToTelegramChunks(input,4096).map((chunk)=>chunk.html).join("")}));' node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.wrap-md.test.ts packages/markdown-core/src/render-aware-chunking.test.ts extensions/slack/src/format.test.ts ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/format.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts pnpm tsgo:extensions autoreview --mode local pnpm openclaw agent --local --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro --session-key agent:default:issue-102162-telegram-url-proof --message 'Reply with exactly this URL and no extra text: https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit' --json --timeout 180 pnpm openclaw message send --channel telegram --target 123456789 --message 'https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit' --dry-run --json ``` Focused test result: 3 Vitest shards passed, covering 129 tests total. `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed. Autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. The DeepSeek local agent run succeeded through the embedded OpenClaw harness with provider `deepseek`, model `deepseek-v4-pro`, and final visible text exactly `https://example.com/wp-admin/post.php?post=100&action=edit`. What was not tested: I did not send to a real Telegram chat or tap the client open-link prompt because this checkout has a bot token but no configured safe target chat. Manual follow-up proof is: send the same bare URL through Telegram with `channels.telegram.richMessages: true`, open it in Telegram Desktop or mobile, and confirm the prompt/tap destination shows `?post=100&action=edit` with a raw `&` separator rather than `&action=edit`. target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.

Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
```

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
